policy_note: Typical exposure labels only. Final posture is adjusted using authorized asset context or Nmap CVSS evidence.

rules.name: ftp
rules.reason: Classic FTP does not encrypt credentials or file data.
rules.recommendation: Confirm {service} on {protocol}/{port} is required. Prefer SFTP or FTPS; otherwise disable it and restrict access.

rules.name: ssh
rules.reason: SSH is powerful remote administration; unrestricted access, passwords, or old software increase risk.
rules.recommendation: Keep {service} on {protocol}/{port} only for approved administrators; use keys or MFA, patch it, and restrict source IPs.

rules.name: telnet
rules.reason: Telnet sends remote-login traffic in plaintext.
rules.recommendation: Disable {service} on {protocol}/{port} and replace it with SSH.

rules.name: smtp
rules.reason: Weak relay and TLS controls can allow spam abuse or mail exposure.
rules.recommendation: Confirm mail-server ownership, prevent open relay, and restrict relay sources.

rules.name: dns
rules.reason: Open recursion or weak DNS configuration can enable amplification or data exposure.
rules.recommendation: Confirm DNS is required, disable open recursion for untrusted clients, and restrict zone transfers.

rules.name: dhcp
rules.reason: DHCP should normally remain on its intended local network only.
rules.recommendation: Confirm DHCP is limited to the intended internal segment and block rogue DHCP traffic.

rules.name: tftp
rules.reason: TFTP generally lacks authentication and encryption.
rules.recommendation: Disable TFTP if unneeded; otherwise isolate it and move sensitive transfers to an authenticated encrypted service.

rules.name: http
rules.reason: HTTP does not encrypt traffic and application flaws may increase the real risk.
rules.recommendation: Redirect {service} on {protocol}/{port} to HTTPS, disable plaintext login, and review the application.

rules.name: pop3
rules.reason: Plain POP3 can expose credentials and mail data.
rules.recommendation: Migrate clients to POP3S and restrict plaintext POP3 during transition.

rules.name: ntp
rules.reason: Misconfigured public NTP can be abused for amplification or disrupt trusted time.
rules.recommendation: Restrict NTP queries to approved networks and remove unnecessary legacy control features.

rules.name: windows_rpc
rules.reason: Windows RPC increases remote-management attack surface when broadly reachable.
rules.recommendation: Restrict RPC to required internal management hosts and block internet exposure.

rules.name: netbios
rules.reason: NetBIOS can expose names, shares, and internal network information.
rules.recommendation: Disable NetBIOS where unused and restrict it to trusted internal segments.

rules.name: imap
rules.reason: Plain IMAP may expose credentials and email data.
rules.recommendation: Require TLS before authentication or migrate users to IMAPS.

rules.name: snmp
rules.reason: Default community strings or SNMPv1/v2c can expose device information.
rules.recommendation: Use SNMPv3, remove default communities, and allow approved monitoring hosts only.

rules.name: ldap
rules.reason: LDAP may be unencrypted and weak access control can expose directory information.
rules.recommendation: Require StartTLS or LDAPS, restrict queries, and review anonymous binds.

rules.name: https
rules.reason: HTTPS provides TLS transport, but application and certificate security still matter.
rules.recommendation: Confirm the HTTPS service is approved and keep certificates, TLS configuration, and application patches current.

rules.name: smb
rules.reason: Public SMB creates a major file-sharing, credential, and ransomware attack surface.
rules.recommendation: Block SMB from the internet; allow only required internal peers and patch supported systems.

rules.name: secure_mail_directory
rules.reason: These services commonly use TLS but still require valid certificates and strong access controls.
rules.recommendation: Confirm TLS and authentication are enforced for {service} on {protocol}/{port}; restrict access to intended clients.

rules.name: database_and_nfs
rules.reason: Database or file services can expose sensitive business data when overexposed.
rules.recommendation: Keep {service} on {protocol}/{port} private, require strong authentication, patch it, and allow only approved application hosts.

rules.name: rdp_vnc
rules.reason: Remote desktop services are common targets for credential attacks and remote compromise.
rules.recommendation: Allow {service} only through VPN or trusted source IPs, require MFA, and disable it if remote administration is not required.

rules.name: redis_elastic_mongo
rules.reason: Improperly exposed data stores can permit data theft, modification, or service compromise.
rules.recommendation: Keep {service} private, require authentication and encryption, patch it, and block public exposure.

rules.name: alternate_web
rules.reason: Alternate web or administration ports need explicit ownership and access review.
rules.recommendation: Confirm the owner of {service} on {protocol}/{port}; restrict administration to trusted peers or VPN.

rules.name: generic_open_service
rules.reason: The service has no dedicated profile; verify its necessity and exposure.
rules.recommendation: Review {service} on {protocol}/{port}, document an owner, and restrict access to required peers.
